<details class="result-group" id="theorem-9-1" open>
<summary><span>Theorem 9.1</span><span class="result-count">3 endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>Under $H_0:\theta=\theta_0$, $T(\theta_0)\xrightarrow{d}N(0,1)$ and $\Pr(\lvert T\rvert\gt c)\to2(1-\Phi(c))$.</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-olshc0linttest-rejectionprob-tendsto">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.olsHC0LinTTest_rejectionProb_tendsto</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 9.1, asymptotic-size half, for the ordinary-OLS HC0 t-test.</strong></p>
<p>The two-sided HC0 t-test "reject if <code>|T| &gt; c</code>" has asymptotic rejection
probability equal to the absolute-standard-normal mass of <code>(c, ∞)</code> — that is,
<code>P[|Z| &gt; c] = 2(1 - Φ(c))</code> for <code>Z ∼ N(0, 1)</code>.</p>
<p>Scope and faithfulness notes:
* This formalizes only claim (b) of Hansen Theorem 9.1 (the rejection-probability
  limit). Claim (a), <code>T(θ₀) →d N(0, 1)</code>, is Hansen Theorem 7.11 and is reused
  via <code>olsHC0LinTStatOrZero_tendstoInDistribution_standardNormal</code>. Claim (c),
  "the test has asymptotic size <code>α</code>", is the calibrated wrapper
  <code>olsHC0LinTTest_rejectionProb_tendsto_alpha</code>.
* The hypotheses are <code>RobustCovarianceConsistencyConditions</code> plus the
  score-weight bounded-in-probability conditions. That package is documented as
  <em>stronger</em> than Hansen's bare Assumption 7.2 (it adds iid-type conditions on
  the score outer products); it is the standard Chapter 7 robust-inference
  hypothesis stack, not a literal rendering of Assumptions 7.2/7.3.
* The t-statistic is evaluated at the true coefficient vector <code>β</code>, so the null
  <code>H₀ : θ = θ₀</code> holds by construction (<code>θ₀ = R'β</code>). The statement is therefore
  Theorem 9.1's conclusion <em>under</em> <code>H₀</code>; it is not a decision rule that
  discriminates <code>H₀</code> from an alternative. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {k : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype k] [inst_1 : DecidableEq k]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [inst_2 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {X : Nat → Ω → k → Real}
  {e y : Nat → Ω → Real},
  HansenEconometrics.RobustCovarianceConsistencyConditions μ X e →
    ∀ (β : k → Real) (R : Matrix Unit k Real),
      (∀ (i : Nat) (ω : Ω), Eq (y i ω) (instHAdd.hAdd (dotProduct (X i ω) β) (e i ω))) →
        (∀ (i : Nat), MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable (X i) μ) →
          (∀ (i : Nat), MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable (e i) μ) →
            (∀ (a b l : k),
                HansenEconometrics.BoundedInProbability μ fun n ω =&gt;
                  HansenEconometrics.sampleScoreCovCrossWeight (HansenEconometrics.stackRegressors X n ω)
                    (HansenEconometrics.stackErrors e n ω) a b l) →
              (∀ (a b l m : k),
                  HansenEconometrics.BoundedInProbability μ fun n ω =&gt;
                    HansenEconometrics.sampleScoreCovQuadraticWeight (HansenEconometrics.stackRegressors X n ω) a b l
                      m) →
                Real.instLT.lt 0
                    (HansenEconometrics.linearRestrictionStdError R (HansenEconometrics.heteroAsymCov μ X e)) →
                  ∀ (crit : Real),
                    Filter.Tendsto
                      (fun n =&gt;
                        MeasureTheory.Measure.instFunLike.coe μ
                          (setOf fun ω =&gt;
                            Real.instLT.lt crit
                              (abs
                                (HansenEconometrics.olsLinearTStatOrZero R
                                  (HansenEconometrics.olsHetCovStar (HansenEconometrics.stackRegressors X n ω)
                                    (HansenEconometrics.stackOutcomes y n ω))
                                  (HansenEconometrics.stackRegressors X n ω) (HansenEconometrics.stackOutcomes y n ω) β
                                  n.cast.sqrt))))
                      Filter.atTop
                      (nhds
                        (MeasureTheory.Measure.instFunLike.coe
                          (MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun x =&gt; abs x) (ProbabilityTheory.gaussianReal 0 1))
                          (Set.Ioi crit)))</code></pre>

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-9-2">
<summary><span>Theorem 9.2</span><span class="result-count">2 endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>Under the multivariate null, $W\xrightarrow{d}\chi_q^2$; a calibrated upper-tail critical value gives asymptotic size $\alpha$.</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-nonlinearolswaldtest-rejectionprob-tendsto-alpha-of-chapter7">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.nonlinearOlsWaldTest_rejectionProb_tendsto_alpha_of_chapter7</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 9.2, nonlinear OLS Wald test from Chapter 7.</strong></p>
<p>This is the theorem-facing robust nonlinear Wald wrapper. The restriction-gap
Gaussian limit is supplied by Chapter 7's nonlinear Delta-method wrapper, and
the plug-in restriction covariance is supplied by Chapter 7's transposed
nonlinear derivative covariance wrapper. The differentiability/Taylor
remainder and Gaussian image-law premises are the corresponding Chapter 7
inputs, not new Chapter 9 CLT assumptions. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {k : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype k] [inst_1 : DecidableEq k]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [inst_2 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {X : Nat → Ω → k → Real}
  {e y : Nat → Ω → Real} {r : Nat} [Fact (instLTNat.lt 0 r)],
  HansenEconometrics.ScoreCLTConditions μ X e →
    ∀ (β : k → Real) (rfun : (k → Real) → Fin r → Real) (θ0 : Fin r → Real) (Rfun : (k → Real) → Matrix k (Fin r) Real),
      (∀ (i : Nat) (ω : Ω), Eq (y i ω) (instHAdd.hAdd (dotProduct (X i ω) β) (e i ω))) →
        (∀ (n : Nat),
            AEMeasurable
              (fun ω =&gt;
                {
                  ofLp :=
                    instHSMul.hSMul n.cast.sqrt
                      (instHSub.hSub
                        (rfun
                          (HansenEconometrics.olsBetaOrZero (HansenEconometrics.stackRegressors X n ω)
                            (HansenEconometrics.stackOutcomes y n ω)))
                        θ0) })
              μ) →
          (MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ
              (fun n ω =&gt;
                instHSub.hSub
                  {
                    ofLp :=
                      instHSMul.hSMul n.cast.sqrt
                        (instHSub.hSub
                          (rfun
                            (HansenEconometrics.olsBetaOrZero (HansenEconometrics.stackRegressors X n ω)
                              (HansenEconometrics.stackOutcomes y n ω)))
                          θ0) }
                  (ContinuousLinearMap.funLike.coe (HansenEconometrics.matrixContinuousLinearMap (Rfun β).transpose)
                    {
                      ofLp :=
                        instHSMul.hSMul n.cast.sqrt
                          (instHSub.hSub
                            (HansenEconometrics.olsBetaOrZero (HansenEconometrics.stackRegressors X n ω)
                              (HansenEconometrics.stackOutcomes y n ω))
                            β) }))
              Filter.atTop fun x =&gt; 0) →
            ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw
                (fun z =&gt;
                  ContinuousLinearMap.funLike.coe (HansenEconometrics.matrixContinuousLinearMap (Rfun β).transpose)
                    { ofLp := (Matrix.inv.inv (HansenEconometrics.popGram μ X)).mulVec z.ofLp })
                (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0
                  (Matrix.instHMulOfFintypeOfMulOfAddCommMonoid.hMul
                    (Matrix.instHMulOfFintypeOfMulOfAddCommMonoid.hMul (Rfun β).transpose
                      (HansenEconometrics.heteroAsymCov μ X e))
                    (Rfun β)))
                (ProbabilityTheory.multivariateGaussian 0 (HansenEconometrics.scoreCovMat μ X e)) →
              ContinuousAt Rfun β →
                (∀ (n : Nat),
                    MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable
                      (fun ω =&gt;
                        Rfun
                          (HansenEconometrics.olsBetaOrZero (HansenEconometrics.stackRegressors X n ω)
                            (HansenEconometrics.stackOutcomes y n ω)))
                      μ) →
                  ∀ {Vhat : Nat → Ω → Matrix k k Real},
                    (∀ (n : Nat), MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable (Vhat n) μ) →
                      (MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure μ Vhat Filter.atTop fun x =&gt;
                          HansenEconometrics.heteroAsymCov μ X e) →
                        (Matrix.instHMulOfFintypeOfMulOfAddCommMonoid.hMul
                              (Matrix.instHMulOfFintypeOfMulOfAddCommMonoid.hMul (Rfun β).transpose
                                (HansenEconometrics.heteroAsymCov μ X e))
                              (Rfun β)).PosDef →
                          ∀ {crit : Real} {alpha : ENNReal},
                            Eq (MeasureTheory.Measure.instFunLike.coe (HansenEconometrics.chiSquared r) (Set.Ioi crit))
                                alpha →
                              Filter.Tendsto
                                (fun n =&gt;
                                  MeasureTheory.Measure.instFunLike.coe μ
                                    (setOf fun ω =&gt;
                                      Real.instLT.lt crit
                                        (HansenEconometrics.nonlinearOlsWaldStatOrZero rfun θ0
                                          (Rfun
                                            (HansenEconometrics.olsBetaOrZero (HansenEconometrics.stackRegressors X n ω)
                                              (HansenEconometrics.stackOutcomes y n ω)))
                                          (Vhat n ω) (HansenEconometrics.stackRegressors X n ω)
                                          (HansenEconometrics.stackOutcomes y n ω) n.cast.sqrt)))
                                Filter.atTop (nhds alpha)</code></pre>
</details>

<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.linMap_olsHC0WaldTest_rejectionProb_tendsto_alpha</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 9.2, robust multivariate Wald test, asymptotic-size <code>α</code> form.</strong></p>
<p>For a linear hypothesis encoded by <code>R</code>, the ordinary-OLS HC0 Wald rule
"reject if <code>W &gt; c</code>" has rejection probability tending to <code>α</code> when the critical
value has <code>χ²(r)</code> upper-tail mass <code>α</code>. The null is encoded by centering at the
true coefficient vector <code>β</code>; the hypotheses reuse Chapter 7's robust feasible
HC moment package, which is stronger than Hansen's bare Assumptions 7.2--7.4. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {k : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype k] [inst_1 : DecidableEq k]
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [inst_2 : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {X : Nat → Ω → k → Real}
  {e y : Nat → Ω → Real} {r : Nat} [Fact (instLTNat.lt 0 r)] (β : k → Real) (R : Matrix (Fin r) k Real),
  HansenEconometrics.RobustFeasibleHCMomentConditions μ X e y β →
    (Matrix.instHMulOfFintypeOfMulOfAddCommMonoid.hMul
          (Matrix.instHMulOfFintypeOfMulOfAddCommMonoid.hMul R (HansenEconometrics.heteroAsymCov μ X e))
          R.transpose).PosDef →
      ∀ {crit : Real} {alpha : ENNReal},
        Eq (MeasureTheory.Measure.instFunLike.coe (HansenEconometrics.chiSquared r) (Set.Ioi crit)) alpha →
          Filter.Tendsto
            (fun n =&gt;
              MeasureTheory.Measure.instFunLike.coe μ
                (setOf fun ω =&gt;
                  Real.instLT.lt crit
                    (HansenEconometrics.linMapOlsWaldStatOrZero R
                      (HansenEconometrics.olsHetCovStar (HansenEconometrics.stackRegressors X n ω)
                        (HansenEconometrics.stackOutcomes y n ω))
                      (HansenEconometrics.stackRegressors X n ω) (HansenEconometrics.stackOutcomes y n ω) β
                      n.cast.sqrt)))
            Filter.atTop (nhds alpha)</code></pre>

<details class="result-group" id="theorem-9-3">
<summary><span>Theorem 9.3</span><span class="result-count">2 endpoints</span></summary>
<div class="result-body">
<div class="textbook-statement"><p>Under homoskedasticity and the null, $W^0\xrightarrow{d}\chi_q^2$.</p></div>
<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-nonlinearolshomowaldtest-rejectionprob-tendsto-alpha-of-chapter7">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.nonlinearOlsHomoWaldTest_rejectionProb_tendsto_alpha_of_chapter7</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p><strong>Hansen Theorem 9.3, nonlinear homoskedastic OLS Wald test from Chapter 7.</strong></p>
<p>The homoskedastic statistic uses the same Chapter 7 nonlinear Delta-method
limit together with Chapter 7's homoskedastic-to-sandwich covariance bridge.

homoskedastic Wald statistic divided by the number of restrictions. Therefore

<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Local-alternative Wald statistic theorem with a named noncentral chi-square limit.</p>
<p>If the scaled restriction gap converges to <code>N(mean, Vtheta)</code> and the plug-in
restriction covariance consistently estimates <code>Vtheta</code>, then Hansen's Wald
quadratic form converges to the noncentral chi-square law with noncentrality
<code>mean' Vtheta⁻¹ mean</code>. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-waldtest-localpower-tendsto-noncentralchisquared">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">theorem</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.waldTest_localPower_tendsto_noncentralChiSquared</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Reusable local-power bridge for the named noncentral chi-square law.</p>
<p>Once the local-alternative Wald statistic has the noncentral chi-square limit
given by <code>restrictionWaldStatOrZero_tendstoInDistribution_noncentralChiSquared</code>,
the upper-tail rejection probability converges to the corresponding noncentral
chi-square tail probability. The frontier-null premise is the only analytic
regularity fact needed to apply the portmanteau rejection-set bridge. </p></div>
<details class="formal-statement"><summary>Formal statement</summary>
<pre><code class="language-lean">∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [inst : MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  {W : Nat → Ω → Real} {r : Nat} {mean : Fin r → Real} {V : Matrix (Fin r) (Fin r) Real} {crit : Real},
  Eq
      (MeasureTheory.Measure.instFunLike.coe (HansenEconometrics.noncentralChiSquared r mean V)
        (frontier (Set.Ioi crit)))
      0 →
    MeasureTheory.TendstoInDistribution W Filter.atTop (fun x =&gt; x) (fun x =&gt; μ)
        (HansenEconometrics.noncentralChiSquared r mean V) →
      Filter.Tendsto (fun n =&gt; MeasureTheory.Measure.instFunLike.coe μ (setOf fun ω =&gt; Real.instLT.lt crit (W n ω)))
        Filter.atTop
        (nhds (MeasureTheory.Measure.instFunLike.coe (HansenEconometrics.noncentralChiSquared r mean V) (Set.Ioi crit)))</code></pre>
</details>

<details class="lean-declaration" id="decl-hanseneconometrics-noncentralchisquared">
<summary><span class="declaration-kind">def</span> <code>HansenEconometrics.noncentralChiSquared</code></summary>
<div class="declaration-body">
<div class="declaration-doc"><p>Noncentral chi-square law induced by a shifted Gaussian Wald quadratic form.</p>
<p>For Hansen's local Wald theorem this is the law of
<code>Z' V⁻¹ Z</code> when <code>Z ∼ N(mean, V)</code>. Its noncentrality parameter is
<code>mean' V⁻¹ mean</code>, exposed separately by <code>noncentralityParam</code>. </p></div>
